description: Separate oblique left and right poses with visible amber backs, ivory end faces, and top caps.

poses.prompt:
Use case: product-mockup. Create a photorealistic isolated game sprite of ONE Japanese mahjong tile STANDING UPRIGHT, viewed OBLIQUELY FROM ABOVE, for a seated opponent's concealed hand in a perspective table. The attached image is only a RESIN MATERIAL / BACK COLOR reference. Do NOT preserve its straight-on camera.
CRITICAL: The large upright BACK PANEL is entirely AMBER YELLOW, without any white stripe on this large back. Show this BACK PANEL prominently, PLUS a smaller IVORY laminated END FACE, PLUS the TOP CAP. THREE visibly different planes with real thickness. This is NOT an edge-on side view and NOT a white-front tile. The printed ivory front faces AWAY toward the seated opponent and must NOT be visible. Real tile proportions: upright height 28 mm, face width 21 mm, thickness 16.5 mm. White core around 65 percent of thickness, amber backing around 35 percent, clean laminate seam on the small end face and top cap.
Camera elevation about 40 degrees and diagonal yaw that makes the amber BACK and near END FACE both clearly visible. All vertical physical edges remain upright in the screen. Detailed molded bevels, rounded corners, softly shaded end face, bright top highlight, darker amber back, tiny natural contact shadow, polished urea resin. The tile must look like a substantial solid three-dimensional block, not a flat rectangle or diagram. Modest lens perspective, almost orthographic sprite, entire object centered with small transparent margin. No symbols, no text, no logos, no floor, no pedestal, no extra objects. Transparent background. Independent generic artwork. LEFT OPPONENT VIEW: the viewer looks at the tile from the table-center side, from its BACK-RIGHT corner. The BROAD AMBER BACK is visible on the RIGHT side of the sprite, facing the center of the table. The SMALL IVORY END FACE is on the LEFT, its amber laminate lip at its right edge. The ivory printed front points LEFT and is hidden. In the game, this tile belongs to a straight row that recedes from LOWER-LEFT toward UPPER-RIGHT. Shape the top cap with that natural oblique direction, with its depth going up and right. Do not make an edge-on white/yellow split face; the amber back must be a separate broad receding vertical face.
